items.title: Frank Tiberi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 30, 2022
items.q: The first record that he made was the “Countdown” record. And of course I mean that was the equal division of the twelve tones. And of course that inspired me.

ctx.x: The first record that he made was the “Countdown” record. And of course I mean that was the equal division of the twelve tones. And of course that inspired me. And I have a concept you know that I’m able to really use the parts of it and to insert it into the “deceptive inserts” I just refer to it as. And I’m able to really create from that, from the

division of the twelve tones, that you know that they are really playing deceptive inserts before the chord is provided, you know, such as piano players do also as well. There are certain things which you can really be able to have a little more fun playing a half step above, that’s pretty well — and of course you have the tritones and but other than that I mean just extracting from the equal divisions of the twelve tones, which is major third, major third, major third.
